assign.request: Reviewer minion for /imagine/game/ realm: ten-second test, primary interaction, layout at 3440, resolve findings in-realm, land.
steps: check layout invariants at 3440 against paging/critique row
re-shoot and verify zero console errors

log.msg: STRANGER: a fantasy exploration game where you click links to walk between named realms/rooms, collecting a lamp/key/lens/sigil to unlock further rooms and eventually a locked gate. MEANT (readme/page.js): a game whose only mechanic is navigation - a realm is a page, a room is a page, an exit is a link to a sibling; nine rooms, four items, one chain, one trade, one way out.

Gap found: the arrival lede explained HOW navigation works (columns/links/persistence) but never said WHAT this is or what you do - no plain takeaway sentence, violating the owner's new law. Fixed by prepending one plain sentence to the lede.

Primary interaction (ui-test): clicked 'Walk in - the Iron Gate' CTA on the 1280 shot. Before/after rects confirmed a new column opened, title 'Iron Gate', correct scene text, url /imagine/game/verge/gate/. Works as promised - no defect here.

Found + fixed a real control/label mismatch: the arrival screen's 3 realm links plus the closing 'Walk in' link are all .imagine-exit (keyboard-numbered per decisions.md round 4), but none shared a counter-reset scope, so Chromium gave each its OWN counter and all four displayed digit '1' - pressing 1 only ever reached The Verge. Verified pre-fix via probe + crop screenshot. Fix: moved counter-reset to .imagine-notes (imagine.css), dropped the redundant reset on the closing row (page.js, .style('--gap','0.4em') to preserve spacing). Verified: labels now read 1/2/3/4 and pressing each digit navigates to the matching room. Zero console errors before and after.

Layout at 3440 (paging/critique row for game, rank 16, score 83): '52% wide - 1424px dead - depth 8 - scroll 1392/1392'. Confirmed visually unchanged (content column still ends well short of 3440, wide grey field to the right). Critique's alt ('launch a persistent inventory or map as a third column') is STILL OPEN, not applied. Left open, not fixed: the module's own doc/decisions.md already deliberated the closest adjacent idea ('fill' for the two written screens, and a second map on the arrival) and rejected both with measured reasoning (row-width jumping between room/non-room screens; two devices saying one thing). A genuine third persistent column is a structural addition beyond a safe same-file fix and conflicts with documented intent - logged as a proposal, not forced. Other two layout invariants pass: leftmost visible content sits at x=48.6px (not 0), and .imagine-lede measures exactly 40.0em (at the cap, not over). No hard-coded spacing constants found where a clamp exists - imagine.css uses em throughout for padding/gap; the two px values (2px map-grid gap, 3px bar-track height) are hairline dividers, not rhythm spacing.

PROPOSED (not applied - needs design work beyond a safe page.js/CSS edit, and revisits a documented decision): add a third, always-visible column at /imagine/game/ showing the map/HUD independent of depth, to use the 1424px dead at 3440. Sketch: split hud()+rail()+map() out of the root Game page's own column into a dedicated sibling region so it survives independent of width:small's 14em cap, OR give the arrival/room columns a width word between large and wide with a max-width tied to a spacing clamp. Either needs new layout work and a fresh measured pass (screens/doc/decisions.md's fill rejection would need re-litigating) - left for the owner's call, not min-ed in under review budget.
Re-shot 1280+3440 post-fix: zero console errors both sizes. Final jpg at framework/ai/2026-09-04/imagine-review/shots/game.jpg, 82860 bytes (quality 70).

assign.outcome:
**The Game's arrival screen now says what it is before it explains how it works, and its keyboard hints stopped lying.** Stranger-vs-meant gap: the lede taught the column-swap mechanic but never said "this is a game" or what to do — fixed with one plain sentence up front. Separately found and fixed a real bug: three realm links plus the closing exit on [`/imagine/game/`](/imagine/game/) all displayed keyboard digit "1" (each `.imagine-exit` got its own un-shared counter scope), so pressing 1 only ever reached The Verge — now reads 1/2/3/4 and each digit verifiably routes to its own room (`imagine.css` `.imagine-notes` counter-reset; `page.js` drops the redundant nested reset). Primary interaction ("Walk in — the Iron Gate") proven with ui-test: opens the right column, right title, right scene. Layout at 3440 unchanged from [`/imagine/paging/critique/`](/imagine/paging/critique/)'s row (52% wide, 1424px dead, score 83) — left open as a proposal, not forced, because the module's own [`doc/decisions.md`](/imagine/game/doc/decisions/) already rejected the two closest adjacent ideas (`fill`, a second map) with measured reasoning; a genuine third persistent column is real design work past a safe same-file edit. Zero console errors, before and after, at 1280/3440.

![](/framework/ai/2026-09-04/imagine-game/landing-1280-fixed.png)

**Fixed:** takeaway sentence added to the arrival lede; exit-counter scope bug (digits now match keyboard behavior).
**Proposed, not applied:** a third persistent map/inventory column to use the 3440 dead space — needs fresh design, conflicts with documented prior rejections.
**Left as-is:** the poetic eyebrow/display composition (`.imagine-open`) — untouched; only the lede's first sentence changed.

log.msg: Self-corrected a fence slip: the counter-reset fix first touched public/imagine/imagine.css, which sits OUTSIDE my realm fence (it is shared by /imagine/, /imagine/team/ and /imagine/game/). Reverted that file to its original state and moved the fix entirely into page.js as an inline .style('counter-reset', 'imagine-exit') on .imagine-notes - verified el.style with a hyphenated CSS property name headless first, then re-ran the digit-navigation checks (1/2/3/4 all still route correctly, zero console errors). imagine.css now shows no diff; every edit is inside public/imagine/game/.
